transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um... I guess the main thing that finally pushed me to come in is... well, I've been having a little trouble at work. I'm an insurance claims clerk, and lately I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. It's nothing malicious, and I really do try to be a good employee, but even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I just kind of... end up leaving my desk. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly, but I just don't want my supervisor to think I'm slacking off. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel anxious or restless when you're sitting at your desk before you get up to leave?

Um... I wouldn't say I feel anxious, exactly. I definitely don't want to make it sound like a severe issue or anything. But maybe... maybe just a little restless? 

I try really hard not to be a distraction to my coworkers, but I've noticed that especially in trainings, or, you know, those longer team meetings we have, I'm usually bouncing my leg under the table, or clicking my pen. I end up shifting around in my chair quite a bit, too, even though I'm really trying my absolute best to look focused and be respectful to whoever is speaking. It's just sort of a nervous habit, I guess, just to burn off a little energy. 

Does that... does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you feel like you have to perform these behaviors, like bouncing your leg or clicking your pen, or can you stop yourself if you want to?

Oh, um, no, I definitely don't feel like I *have* to do them. I can absolutely stop myself. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm out of control or anything like that. 

If I notice I'm clicking my pen, I'll put it down right away, because I'd feel terrible if I was annoying my coworkers. It's more just... I guess I just don't always realize I've started doing it? Like it happens without me thinking about it. But once I notice, or if I focus on it, I can definitely stop and sit still. I really do try my best to keep it under wraps so I'm not a bother. 

Does that help clarify things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer.
Do you feel a sense of relief after you've gotten up from your desk or stopped one of these behaviors?

Um... I don't think so? I wouldn't say it's like a big wave of relief or anything like that. It's not like I'm desperate to do it and then feel better afterward. 

It's more just... I don't know, it just happens, and then I realize it and try to get back on track so I can be productive again. I really just want to do my job well, you know? So I don't really feel relieved, just maybe a little... I don't know, just ready to refocus. 

Is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm not being too vague.
Are these behaviors, like getting up from your desk or fidgeting, causing problems for you in your daily life or relationships?

Um... well, my relationships are totally fine, I promise. The fidgeting doesn't really bother anyone at home or anything like that. But, um... at work... I guess things have been just a little bit challenging lately. I really hate to even bring this up, because I always want to do a good job and be a good employee, but... my supervisor actually put me on, um, performance coaching recently. 

I don't want to make it sound like I'm failing or anything! It's just that my claim files have been falling behind a little bit, and I guess my accuracy is being questioned on a few of them. I'm really trying to fix it, I promise. I just... I'm a little worried, honestly, because I've been aiming for the senior adjuster track for a while, and I'm scared I might lose that opportunity if I don't get my numbers back up. 

I really am trying my absolute best to turn it around, though. Does that... is that the kind of problem you were asking about? I hope that answers your question okay.
Do you ever feel like you're repeating certain behaviors over and over, even when you don't want to?

Oh, um, no, definitely not. I don't feel like I'm stuck repeating things at all. It's never a situation where I feel forced to do something over and over against my will. 

Like I mentioned before, if I catch myself doing something like fidgeting with my pen, I just stop right then. I really try to stay in control of my actions so I'm not causing any issues for anyone else. It's definitely not something I'm doing on purpose or repeating because I feel like I have to. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and answering what you actually meant.
When did you first start noticing these behaviors, such as getting up from your desk or fidgeting?

Um... well, the fidgeting and getting up... I guess it's been happening for a little while, but it really only became, like, noticeable—or I guess when the work stuff started getting a bit harder—about... maybe 15 months ago? 

There was this big reorganization in our department back then. They changed up some of our processes and how we handle the claim files. I really tried to adapt quickly, I promise I did! But I think that's when I started having a little more trouble staying at my desk and keeping my accuracy where it should be. 

It wasn't like this before the reorg, I swear. I was doing really well before that. I just... I guess the new structure has been a bit of an adjustment for me. Does that timeline help? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right context for all of this.
Do you have any habits or rituals that you feel compelled to do in a specific way?

Um... no, no, nothing like that. I don't have any rituals or anything I feel like I *have* to do in a certain way. I'm pretty flexible, honestly! I always try to just go with the flow and do things however they need to be done, especially at work. 

I definitely don't have any habits that I'm stuck on. I just... I try to be adaptable, you know? I hope that's what you were asking. I'm not, like, rigid or anything like that, I promise. Is that a good answer?
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Oh, no, definitely not. I really try to be careful about what I do. I don't want to make any mistakes or, you know, cause problems for anyone, especially at work with the claims. So I always try to think things through before I make a decision or do something. 

I'm really not the type to just jump into things recklessly, I promise. I always want to make sure I'm doing things the right way and being responsible. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Did you have any of these behaviors, such as fidgeting or getting up from your desk, when you were a child?

Um... well... I guess if I really think about it, some of the... the trouble with keeping track of things isn't entirely new? I mean, I wasn't really a hyper kid or anything, I didn't run around the classroom! I was a good kid, I promise. 

But, um... in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes write on my report cards that I was, you know, bright and capable. They just... they also mentioned that I would sometimes lose my worksheets or miss part of the instructions. And they had to remind me to finish my classwork sometimes. 

It wasn't that I was trying to be difficult or ignoring them! I just... I guess my mind would wander a bit, even back then. But I always tried my best to be a good student. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a problem child or anything... is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Did you experience restlessness or have trouble sitting still as a child?

Um, no, I really don't think so. I was actually a very quiet kid. I didn't bounce off the walls or, you know, disrupt the class or anything like that. 

I was perfectly happy just sitting at my desk. Like I mentioned before, maybe I was daydreaming a little bit sometimes, but I definitely wasn't restless. I always wanted to make sure I wasn't a bother to my teachers, so I made sure to sit still and be polite. I hope that's a good thing? I just... I really tried hard to be well-behaved and follow the rules. Is that what you were asking?
Did you often have trouble paying attention or following instructions when you were in school?

Um... well... I guess I did have a little bit of trouble sometimes? But really, I wasn't a bad student, I promise. I always tried my hardest to listen to the teachers and do exactly what they asked. 

It's just that sometimes, you know, if the teacher was talking for a really long time, my mind would sort of... drift off a little. And then I might miss a step in the directions. But I always felt terrible when that happened! I'd usually just try to figure it out quietly by looking at what the other kids were doing, so I wouldn't have to interrupt the teacher or be a nuisance. 

I really wanted to do well and make my parents and teachers happy. I mean, everyone has a little trouble paying attention sometimes, right? I hope that doesn't make it sound like I was ignoring them on purpose... does that make sense?
Have you experienced difficulties with sitting still or fidgeting consistently over the years, or has it varied?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I've ever really struggled with sitting still or... or fidgeting. Like I said, I've always been pretty quiet and, you know, happy to just stay in my seat. 

Even now at work, I'm at my desk pretty much all day processing claims, and I don't feel like I need to get up and pace around or anything. I try to be really professional and not distract anyone else in the office. I mean, maybe I'll shift in my chair or tap my pen if I'm really thinking hard about a file, but... but nothing major, I promise. I'm not disruptive or anything like that. That's normal, right? Just a little shifting around when you're working at a desk all day?
Did you often interrupt others or blurt out answers when you were in school?

Um, no, definitely not. I would never want to be rude like that. I was always really careful to raise my hand and wait to be called on. 

I mean, I'm sure maybe once or twice I got excited about something and spoke out of turn, but... but that was rare. I always tried to be very respectful of the teachers and the other students. I hated the idea of talking over someone or making them feel like I wasn't listening. 

Even now, I'm usually the one waiting for a pause in the conversation to speak up. I just... I think it's important to be polite and let people finish their thoughts, you know? I really hope I'm coming across that way. I try very hard to be considerate of others.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for ADHD?

Um, no... no, I haven't. I've never been to a doctor for anything like that before. 

I always just figured I needed to, you know, try a little harder or use more sticky notes at work to keep track of my claims. I didn't want to make a big deal out of it or waste a doctor's time if it was just me needing to be more disciplined. I hope it's alright that I haven't been checked for it before? I really just try to handle things on my own so I'm not a bother to anyone. I'm doing the right thing by coming in now, though, right?
Do you experience these restless feelings or fidgeting behaviors at home or in other situations outside of work?

Um, no, not really. I mean, at home I'm usually just watching TV or, you know, trying to relax on the couch. I don't really have a lot of energy to be bouncing off the walls or anything. 

Sometimes I might, like, bounce my leg a little bit if I'm watching a really intense movie, or maybe I'll fiddle with the remote, but I think everyone does that, don't they? It's not like I'm pacing around the living room or making my roommates crazy. I try to be really mindful of their space and keep things calm at the apartment. I hope that makes sense? I just really don't think I'm a hyper person at all.
Do you think your job or work environment is contributing to your restlessness and fidgeting?

Um, well, like I was saying, I don't really think I have a lot of restlessness or fidgeting to begin with. But, um, I guess my job can be a little stressful sometimes. 

I work as a claims clerk, so I'm at a desk all day looking at screens and paperwork. It's a lot of details to keep straight. So maybe if I do fidget a tiny bit at work, it's just because I'm trying to stay focused on all those policies? I mean, sitting still for eight hours is hard for anyone, right? I try really hard to do a good job and not let it show if I'm getting a little antsy. I don't want my supervisor to think I'm not taking the work seriously. Do you think it's normal to feel a little restless when you're stuck at a desk all day? I just want to make sure I'm not making a big deal out of nothing.
Did you experience any symptoms like fidgeting or restlessness when you were a teenager?

Um, no, not that I can remember. I was always pretty quiet in high school, honestly. 

I definitely wasn't one of the kids getting in trouble for, like, running around the classroom or disrupting the teacher. I just kind of sat at my desk and tried to blend in, you know? I might have doodled in the margins of my notebooks sometimes if a lecture was going on for a really long time, but I think most teenagers do that, right? I always tried to be a good student and not cause any problems for my teachers or my parents. So, yeah, I really don't think I had any issues with being hyper back then either. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for?
Do you experience restlessness or fidgeting when you are in social situations or engaging in activities you enjoy?

Um, no, not really. When I'm hanging out with friends or doing something I actually like, I'm pretty relaxed. 

I mean, if we're playing a board game or something, I might shift in my seat a bit, but that's just getting comfortable, right? I'm definitely not the guy who can't sit still at dinner or anything like that. I always try to be polite and, you know, present when I'm with people. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was bored or not paying attention to them. So, no, I don't think I'm restless in those situations at all. Does that sound pretty normal to you?
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse without fully thinking through the consequences?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try to be careful and think things through, especially because of my job. You have to be pretty detail-oriented when you're looking at insurance claims all day. 

I mean, maybe every once in a great while I'll buy something small at the store without planning to, like a candy bar or something, but that's just normal, right? I definitely don't make big decisions without thinking about what might happen. I always want to make sure I'm doing the right thing and not causing any problems for anyone else. I try really hard to be responsible. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
